verdict.rationale: Maritime's docs say every API key carries scopes and recommend giving each subsystem the narrowest key it needs. A computers-only key is concretely documented and is refused on every other endpoint, so least-privilege credentials exist for one surface. Beyond that one scope, the depth of scoping is unproven: missing for 10: an enumerated scope catalog beyond `computers`, per-agent or per-resource key scoping, key expiry or rotation (docs say long-lived keys never expire), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Every key carries scopes. Hand a subsystem the _narrowest_ key it needs. A leaked key can then only do what its scope allows.
To hand out a key that reaches computers and nothing else, create a **Computers key** in the Computers section of Settings, API keys
a key whose only scope is `computers` is refused on every other Maritime endpoint
